findings_digest.claim: FIX 2026Q2 backlog 達 $14.06B，較 2025Q2 的 $8.12B 成長約73%（YoY 近翻倍，季增13%），同期公司宣布2026年將預製/模組化產能擴大30%以因應資料中心需求，顯示其在資料中心 MEP 承包需求中持續擴大承接量而非流失。
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results (BusinessWire, 2026-07-23); Yahoo Finance "Comfort Systems USA Taps Data Center Boom With Modular Capacity Ramp"

findings_digest.claim: 產業結構面：具備財力、保證金(bonding)能力與 mission-critical 經驗、足以承接超大型資料中心案的專業機電承包商供給有限，現有專業廠商在手訂單/產能缺口達現有承接能力的3倍，且美國營建業電機/HVAC技術工缺口2026年預估逾50萬人，形成進入障礙，短期內未見具體新進入者搶單案例。
findings_digest.source: iRecruit "Hyperscale Data Center Buildout 2026: AI, Power, Talent"

findings_digest.claim: 主要上市同業為 EMCOR、Limbach、Legence（均為公開策略性公司而非PE支持的新進入者）；FIX 與 EMCOR 過去約25年皆為穩健但溫和成長型態，搜尋結果未揭露任何具體份額百分比消長數字或新進入者/替代供應商搶單案例。
findings_digest.source: Facilities Dive "How MEP contractor Comfort Systems USA leveraged Lego-like model to drive 15x growth"; Yahoo Finance "Comfort Systems vs. EMCOR: Which HVAC/MEP Stock is the Better Buy Now?"

findings_digest.claim: FIX 最大單一客戶占2024年度合併營收13.3%、占2024年底應收帳款17.7%（2023年度為14%），個別客戶層級集中度屬中等，未見該客戶或其他大型客戶改採第二供應商或轉自製(in-house)的揭露。
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA FY2024 10-K，轉引自 Zacks/TradingView "Comfort Systems' Tech Boom: Growth Engine or Concentration Risk?"

findings_digest.claim: 先進科技相關專案（主要為資料中心建設）占FIX 2026年第一季總營收56%，顯示終端市場/客戶集中度風險已高度集中在少數超大型雲端業者身上（非分散型傳統客戶群）。
findings_digest.source: Zacks/Yahoo Finance "Comfort Systems' Tech Boom: Growth Engine or Concentration Risk?"

findings_digest.claim: 產業結構層面（非FIX專屬揭露）：超大型資料中心業主(hyperscaler)近年普遍轉向 Owner-Furnished Equipment(OFE)模式，直接採購長前置期機電設備（switchgear、發電機、UPS、冷水主機）並提前18個月鎖單以取得量價折扣，繞過機電承包商的設備採購毛利，屬結構性『業主自行採購／繞道』趨勢，壓縮承包商可攫取的利潤範圍；未查得FIX本身客戶被證實改採第二供應商的具體案例。
findings_digest.source: Linesight "Hyperscale data center construction: A program approach to MEP subcontractor procurement"; iRecruit "Hyperscale Data Center Buildout 2026"

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA's data center construction work accounted for 56% of total revenue in Q1 2026, and technology-sector customers (largely hyperscale cloud providers) rose to 58.7% of revenue in Q2 2026, up from ~31% the prior year — meaning the company's revenue is now majority-concentrated in a small number of hyperscaler end customers.
findings_digest.source: Investing.com — 'Comfort Systems Q1 2026 slides: revenue surges 56% on tech demand' and 'Comfort Systems Q2 2026 slides: revenue tops $3B, backlog hits $14B'

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA's 10-K (filed 2026-02-19) discloses customer concentration as a material risk factor: a significant portion of revenue comes from a limited number of customers, posing risk if these customers reduce or terminate contracts. Historically (pre-AI-buildout 10-Ks), no single customer accounted for more than 3% of consolidated revenue, but the mix has shifted materially toward technology/data-center customers since.
findings_digest.source: TradingView News — 'COMFORT SYSTEMS USA INC SEC 10-K Report'

findings_digest.claim: FIX's largest end customers are hyperscale cloud providers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta) that collectively guided to ~$725B combined 2026 capex (Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft ~$190B, Google $175-185B, Meta $115-135B) and a projected $934.5B in 2027 — all four are investment-grade, cash-generative balance sheets, indicating low near-term counterparty credit risk despite customer concentration.
findings_digest.source: valueaddvc.com — '$725B AI Capex 2026: Amazon, Google, Meta & Microsoft'; CNBC — 'Tech AI spending approaches $700 billion in 2026, cash taking big hit'

findings_digest.claim: Amazon is projected to turn free-cash-flow negative in 2026 due to the scale of its AI/data-center capex commitments, a data point cited alongside the hyperscaler capex figures as a potential early stress signal on customer capital allocation even though balance-sheet credit quality remains high.
findings_digest.source: CNBC — 'Tech AI spending approaches $700 billion in 2026, cash taking big hit'

findings_digest.claim: Roughly 30-50% of planned 2026 AI data center capacity is projected to slip to 2028 due to power grid interconnection queues and construction bottlenecks; approximately 7GW of the 12GW of U.S. data center capacity announced for 2026 has been canceled or delayed.
findings_digest.source: tech-insider.org — 'U.S. AI Data Center Delays: 7 GW Capacity Crisis [2026]'

findings_digest.claim: Grid interconnection delays now stretch 4-5 years and transformer lead times (tied to ITC import data) run roughly 5 years, which converts what looked like a 2026-2027 cyclical capacity crunch into a late-decade structural bottleneck; data centers are driving 55% of U.S. electricity demand growth.
findings_digest.source: Inflect — 'Data Center Power Shortage 2026: Why Grid Capacity Is Now the Bigger Constraint Than GPUs'

findings_digest.claim: CBRE reports that despite record data center construction activity, no contiguous data-center space of 5MW or more will be available anywhere during 2026, and the next large contiguous projects are not expected to come online until late 2027 at the earliest — construction supply is not catching up with demand in the near term.
findings_digest.source: Data Center Frontier — 'CBRE: Record Data Center Construction Fails to Ease Capacity Crunch'

findings_digest.claim: FIX's backlog reached $14.06 billion as of Q2 2026 (up ~80.8% y/y at one point in the cycle), with management citing continued strength in technology bookings and a pipeline of larger modular/data-center projects extending into 2027 and 2028; a meaningful portion of Q4 2025 modular bookings is scheduled to be performed primarily in 2027.
findings_digest.source: Investing.com — 'Comfort Systems Q2 2026 slides: revenue tops $3B, backlog hits $14B'; Simply Wall St — 'AI Data Center Backlog Expansion Might Change The Case For Investing In Comfort Systems USA (FIX)'

findings_digest.claim: Analysts flag tight skilled-labor markets (electricians, pipefitters, mechanical trades) as a risk that could constrain Comfort Systems USA's own ability to convert its record backlog into delivered, margin-consistent revenue — a supply-side bottleneck on FIX's execution capacity, not just end-market demand.
findings_digest.source: Simply Wall St — 'Comfort Systems USA Rides Data Center Boom With Record Margins And Backlog'

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA's FY2025 10-K discloses standard industry regulatory exposure (engineering/construction/service-technician licensing, building and MEP codes, government-project bidding/procurement rules, wage-and-hour law, worker-safety and environmental regulation) and states the company believes it holds required licenses and is in substantial compliance; no antitrust, monopoly, or breakup proceeding is disclosed.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR, filed ~2026-02-20)

findings_digest.claim: Industry commentary on the 2026 data-center/mechanical construction 'industrial supercycle' flags the phasedown of PFAS-based coolants and sealants (widely used in specialized cooling systems) as an emerging environmental-regulatory risk for the sector, with compliant players positioned to capture share as the rules tighten.
findings_digest.source: FinancialContent — "Comfort Systems USA Shares Hit Record Highs as 'Industrial Supercycle' Ignites Infrastructure Demand"

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA's FY2025 10-K states that the company, its suppliers, and its customers import raw materials, components, and other products from foreign suppliers, and that trade restrictions, a trade war, or tariff/trade-agreement policy changes could adversely affect demand, costs, customers, suppliers and the broader U.S. economy; direct purchase of commodities and finished products (ductwork, pipe, valves, fittings, electrical wire, conduit, fixtures, fabricated steel/sheet metal) comprises 40%-45% of average project cost, and the company has procedures aimed at reducing commodity cost exposure including tariff-driven costs.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR, filed ~2026-02-20)

findings_digest.claim: A White House proclamation effective June 8, 2026 through December 31, 2027 modified Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper: the 25% duty remains the standard rate (now applied to the full customs value including derivative products, with new derivative items such as steel racks added to scope), while eligibility for a reduced 15% tariff rate was expanded to include residential HVAC systems/components, agricultural equipment and certain industrial machinery.
findings_digest.source: White & Case LLP, "United States modifies steel, aluminum, and copper Section 232 tariffs"; corroborated by Kintetsu World Express and Green Worldwide Shipping client advisories

findings_digest.claim: The U.S. and China reached a preliminary trade agreement on 2025-10-30 easing tensions, and USTR Section 301 China tariffs were suspended for one year starting 2025-11-10 (with China suspending its retaliatory tariffs in kind), reducing near-term U.S.-China trade/tariff escalation risk broadly.
findings_digest.source: Morrison Foerster, "United States and China Reach Trade Agreement: Takeaways for Export and Supply Chain Controls"

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA is a U.S.-based field-installation contractor (no offshore manufacturing of its own), but a large share of its critical long-lead equipment — large power transformers and switchgear used on the data-center/technology projects that now dominate its backlog — is imported, with U.S. imports of high-power transformers from China surging from under 1,500 units in 2022 to over 8,000 units in 2025, and combined U.S. imports of transformers, switchgear and lithium-ion batteries growing from $33.2B (2020) to $77.1B (2025), exposing the electrical-equipment supply chain FIX depends on to concentrated Chinese-manufacturing exposure.
findings_digest.source: Coalition for a Prosperous America, "America's AI Boom Has a Trade Policy Blind Spot"

findings_digest.claim: Lead times for large power transformers have stretched to as long as five years (versus 24-30 months pre-2020), and as of April 2026 nearly half of U.S. data-center capacity planned for the year faces delay or cancellation risk tied to shortages of transformers, switchgear and batteries — a single-point-of-failure exposure for FIX because its technology-segment revenue recognition and schedule-driven project execution depend on timely delivery of this same long-lead electrical gear.
findings_digest.source: webhosting.today, "Up to Half of US Data Centers Planned for 2026 Will Not Be Built on Time — Chinese Electrical Equipment Is the Constraint No One Planned For"; corroborated by PowerMag, "Transformers in 2026: Shortage, Scramble, or Self-Inflicted Crisis?"

findings_digest.claim: Copper, a core transformer input, became subject to a 50% Section 232 tariff under the April 2026 expansion of steel/aluminum/copper duties, and Section 232 tariffs on Chinese electrical equipment further raise landed costs for the switchgear/transformer supply chain FIX's projects rely on.
findings_digest.source: Coalition for a Prosperous America, "America's AI Boom Has a Trade Policy Blind Spot"

findings_digest.claim: Technology (data centers and semiconductor/chip manufacturing) end market accounted for 57.6% of Comfort Systems USA's year-to-date 2026 revenue, up from a much smaller historical share, driven by data-center and advanced-manufacturing project demand; combined with manufacturing (17.5%), industrial-related end markets made up 75.1% of YTD 2026 revenue.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA Q2 2026 earnings release / 10-Q (SEC EDGAR) as reported by TradingView/StockTitan summaries

findings_digest.claim: Company backlog reached a record $12.45 billion at Q1 2026 (up 80.8% YoY from $6.89B) and grew further to $14.06 billion at Q2 2026, with same-store sequential backlog growth driven primarily by increased technology-sector project bookings at the company's Texas electrical operation (+$1.00B) and Texas modular operation (+$510.2M); management cited continued strength in technology bookings and pipeline, including larger modular and data-center projects extending into 2027 and 2028.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA Q1/Q2 2026 earnings releases (investors.comfortsystemsusa.com); TradingView, "Can Comfort Systems' $12.45B Backlog Sustain Its Growth Momentum?"

findings_digest.claim: Institutional end markets (healthcare, education, government) contributed 16.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (healthcare ~7%, education ~5%, government ~4% of YTD 2026 revenue), while commercial end markets (office, retail, multi-family) contributed just 7.1% of Q2 2026 revenue (office buildings ~3% of YTD 2026 revenue) — both segments now a small and shrinking share of the mix as technology/industrial demand has come to dominate.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA Q2 2026 investor materials, as reported by StockTitan/MarketScreener summaries

findings_digest.claim: First-half 2026 total company revenue rose 53.1% YoY to $6.13 billion (Q1 2026 revenue alone rose 56.5% YoY to $2.87 billion), with management attributing the acceleration specifically to technology-sector demand for data centers and semiconductor fabrication facilities.
findings_digest.source: Comfort Systems USA First Quarter 2026 and Second Quarter 2026 Results press releases (investors.comfortsystemsusa.com)

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA is itself driving the shift to volumetric modular/prefabricated MEP construction (building systems in its own facilities so field crews mainly assemble pre-made modules on site), and is expanding this modular capacity by 30% in 2026 toward a 4-5 million sq ft target to meet AI/cloud/HPC data center demand — i.e. the company is the adopter/leader of the substitute method rather than a target being disrupted by it.
findings_digest.source: Facilities Dive, "How MEP contractor Comfort Systems USA leveraged Lego-like model to drive 15x growth" (https://www.facilitiesdive.com/news/how-mep-contractor-comfort-systems-usa-leveraged-lego-like-model-to-drive-1/804611/); Comfort Systems USA 8-K FY2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001035983/000110465926089781/tm2621841d1_ex99-1.htm)

findings_digest.claim: Highly modularized data center projects achieve schedule reductions of 30-50% versus conventional builds, and the global modular data center market is projected to grow at a 17.4% CAGR from 2025-2030; operators report plans to deploy power modules (77%) and cooling modules (69%) as standard practice.
findings_digest.source: CMIC Global, "Key Data Center Construction Trends in 2026" (https://cmicglobal.com/resources/article/data-center-construction-trends); AIRSYS North America, "Data Center Trends & Cooling Strategies to Watch in 2026" (https://airsysnorthamerica.com/data-center-trends-cooling-strategies-to-watch-in-2026/)

findings_digest.claim: As GPU rack density rises (average rack power climbing from 8kW in 2024 to 15kW in 2026), liquid cooling adoption is rising in lockstep with thermal capacities up to 4x greater than air cooling; this represents a technology shift within the mechanical scope of data center work rather than a bypass of mechanical contractors — hyperscalers self-perform civil work but continue to outsource mechanical and electrical scopes to specialists, with mechanical infrastructure spend growing fastest (9.87%) among data center construction categories in 2025-2026.
findings_digest.source: Grit Insurance, "How the Data Center Boom Is Reshaping Contractor Bonding" (https://gritinsurance.com/blog/data-center-construction-boom-contractor-bonding); AIRSYS North America 2026 cooling trends report (https://airsysnorthamerica.com/data-center-trends-cooling-strategies-to-watch-in-2026/)

findings_digest.claim: CFO Bill George stated on the Q2 2026 earnings call: "Because we sell directly to the hyperscalers and to the most important intermediaries, we have a really good view on what they're thinking, what they're planning," indicating Comfort Systems' go-to-market is structured around direct relationships with hyperscale end-customers and key intermediaries rather than solely through traditional layered general-contractor subcontracting.
findings_digest.source: Investing.com, "Earnings call transcript: Comfort Systems USA tops Q2 2026 estimates, stock slips" (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-comfort-systems-usa-tops-q2-2026-estimates-stock-slips-93CH-4812224)

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems has shifted a substantial share of production from traditional on-site trade labor to a volumetric modular ("Lego-like") off-site fabrication model — building systems into its own facilities so field crews primarily assemble pre-made modules — and this business-model shift is cited by an industry analyst (Tim Mulrooney) as central to the company's outsized valuation growth since 2021.
findings_digest.source: Facilities Dive, "How MEP contractor Comfort Systems USA leveraged Lego-like model to drive 15x growth" (https://www.facilitiesdive.com/news/how-mep-contractor-comfort-systems-usa-leveraged-lego-like-model-to-drive-1/804611/)

findings_digest.claim: Hyperscalers are vertically integrating (self-performing) civil construction scope while continuing to hire specialist contractors for mechanical and electrical scopes, compressing overall project schedules from 24 to 18 months and reducing general contractors' addressable value by roughly 25% — a channel restructuring that thins the traditional GC layer while preserving/growing the role of direct mechanical/electrical specialists.
findings_digest.source: Grit Insurance, "How the Data Center Boom Is Reshaping Contractor Bonding" (https://gritinsurance.com/blog/data-center-construction-boom-contractor-bonding)

findings_digest.claim: 分析師共識評等為「Strong Buy」，平均目標價約 $2,197（8–10 位分析師，區間 $1,910–$2,500，中位數約 $2,166），對比 numbers.price_at_dd（$1,610.34）隱含約 30–39% 上檔空間
findings_digest.source: stockanalysis.com — Comfort Systems USA (FIX) Stock Forecast & Analyst Price Targets (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/fix/forecast/); 同期 investing.com consensus estimates 頁面交叉確認

findings_digest.claim: 2026 年 Q2（calendar Q2）財報：營收 $3.27B（YoY +50%，首次單季破 $30 億），EPS $12.53，淨利年增 91% 至 $441.6M；管理層將全年同店營收成長 guidance 上修至「中至高 30% 區間」（先前為中至高 20% 區間）
findings_digest.source: Yahoo Finance — Comfort Systems USA Inc (FIX) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Highlights (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/comfort-systems-usa-inc-fix-230035794.html); TIKR blog — Comfort Systems' Q2 Earnings Crossed $3 Billion (https://www.tikr.com/blog/comfort-systems-q2-earnings-crossed-3-billion-for-the-first-time-the-backlog-says-more-is-coming)

findings_digest.claim: 在制文件中積壓訂單（backlog）於 Q2 2026 季底達歷史新高 $14.1B，年增 73%、季增 13%，其中 $5.6B 的年增來自既有業務（非併購貢獻）
findings_digest.source: Investing.com — Comfort Systems Q2 2026 slides: revenue tops $3B, backlog hits $14B (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/comfort-systems-q2-2026-slides-revenue-tops-3b-backlog-hits-14b-93CH-4812234)

findings_digest.claim: 多家券商於 Q2 財報後上修目標價：UBS 由 $2,125 上調至 $2,225；KeyBanc 由 $2,004 上調至 $2,110（理由為上修營收/獲利估計）；Goldman Sachs 以 Buy 評等、$2,159 目標價新啟動覆蓋
findings_digest.source: Benzinga analyst ratings aggregation for FIX (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FIX/analyst-ratings); WallStreetZen FIX stock forecast (https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nyse/fix/stock-forecast)

findings_digest.claim: 管理層在 Q2 法說會中提示下半年（尤其 Q4）成長將因比較基期轉難而放緩，市場對「沒有進一步加速」的訊號有失望反應
findings_digest.source: TIKR blog — Comfort Systems' Q2 Earnings Crossed $3 Billion for the First Time (https://www.tikr.com/blog/comfort-systems-q2-earnings-crossed-3-billion-for-the-first-time-the-backlog-says-more-is-coming)

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX) acquired Feyen Zylstra Holdings, LLC (electrical design/install/maintenance for industrial, technology and healthcare clients, Michigan-based) and Meisner Electric, Inc. (electrical design/install/renovation/greenfield construction across healthcare, commercial and government markets, Florida-based), effective October 1, 2025.
findings_digest.source: Tracxn — List of 21 Acquisitions by Comfort Systems USA (Aug 2026); corroborated by Comfort Systems 8-K filings (SEC EDGAR CIK 1035983, filing accession 000110465925101818, dated 2025-10-23)

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA integrated Right Way Plumbing and Mechanical (mechanical services) into its operations effective May 1, 2025, as part of its bolt-on M&A strategy; the company completed a total of five acquisitions during 2025.
findings_digest.source: Yahoo Finance — "Could Comfort Systems' Acquisitions Fuel a Multi-Year Rally?"

findings_digest.claim: A former Comfort Systems USA employee filed a proposed ERISA class action on February 4, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas, alleging the company's 401(k) plan retained a risky, underperforming stable-value/guaranteed-income fund from Empower Annuity Insurance Co. (holding over $100 million in plan assets as of 2023) that let Empower earn excessive profits at participants' expense. This is a retirement-plan fiduciary-duty suit, not a securities-fraud class action against FIX stock.
findings_digest.source: Bloomberg Law — "Comfort Systems Sued Over 401(k) Plan's Stable Value Investment"

findings_digest.claim: Industry-wide (not FIX-specific): a report finds nearly half of U.S. data centers scheduled for completion in 2026 face delays or cancellation, driven by permitting bottlenecks, power-grid shortfalls, and community resistance — a backdrop risk to FIX's data-center-driven backlog (backlog was $12.45B per Q1 2026 report vs $6.89B a year earlier).
findings_digest.source: MSN/wire report — "Report: Nearly 1/2 of U.S. data centers due in 2026 face delays or cancelation"; backlog figures via Seeking Alpha coverage of Comfort Systems Q1 2026 results

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems USA acquired Feyen Zylstra Holdings, LLC and Meisner Electric, Inc., effective October 1, 2025, expanding electrical services presence in Michigan and Florida across industrial, technology, healthcare, commercial and government end markets.
findings_digest.source: Tracxn — List of 21 Acquisitions by Comfort Systems USA (Aug 2026); SEC EDGAR 8-K accession 000110465925101818 (filed 2025-10-23)

findings_digest.claim: Comfort Systems integrated Right Way Plumbing and Mechanical effective May 1, 2025, one of five total acquisitions completed by the company in 2025.
findings_digest.source: Yahoo Finance — "Could Comfort Systems' Acquisitions Fuel a Multi-Year Rally?"

findings_digest.claim: A former Comfort Systems USA employee filed a proposed ERISA class action on February 4, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas over the company's 401(k) plan's stable-value/guaranteed-income fund (Empower Annuity Insurance Co.), alleging excessive risk, subpar returns, and excessive fees benefiting Empower; fund held >$100M in plan assets as of 2023. This is an ERISA fiduciary-duty suit, not a securities-fraud class action against FIX stock.
findings_digest.source: Bloomberg Law — "Comfort Systems Sued Over 401(k) Plan's Stable Value Investment"
